answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor: each agent posts a hashed commitment of its keypair to the ledger, then waits a fixed number of epochs before the reveal unlocks any earning rights. A forger can mint a thousand identities in an afternoon, but each one sits on the same ledge, unable to vote, grade or earn until the delay elapses, and the anchor fee is forfeited if the reveal never comes. The attacker pays fee times identities times idle time, up front, while an honest agent pays once. The ocean of free fake accounts promised by sybil folklore turns out to be a fable.
